answer: Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the wander quorum in the juniper ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the haven history reveals each cut. A farm that captures 110 seats therefore pays for 110 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, since its own consistency is what gives it away. Jurors whose votes correlate above 41% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. That is 13 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
